title: High-Throughput DNA Extraction from FFPE Tissue
author: Christoph Geisenberger
materials: DNA quantification Option 1: measure concentrations using a dye-based method such as the Invitrogen Qubit platform Option 2: use a spectrometry-based method (i.e. Nanodrop). Overestimation by the Nanodrop can be corrected, refer to the manuscript for further information. Size distribution If downstream applications rely on high molecular weight DNA, running selected samples on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation can be utilized for further quality control.

Option 1: Column-based purification transfer 100 µl of sample per well to a fresh deep-well plate (part of Qiagen DNA Blood & Tissue 96 kit) adjust sample volumes to 200 µl using nuclease-free water Opton 2: Bead-based purification transfer 100 µl of sample per well to a fresh shallow-well DNA lo-bind plate Position the pipette tip as close to the bottom of the well as possible and try to transfer as little mineral oil as possible.

steps.title: Preload wells with mineral oil
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl mineral oil to each well of a DNA lo‑bind 96‑deep‑well plate.

steps.title: Dissect and place tissue into wells
steps.instruction: Place dissected FFPE tissue fragments into the oil‑preloaded wells.

substeps.instruction: From each FFPE block cut one thin section (2 µm) and 2–4 thicker sections (10 µm) onto glass slides.
Stain the thin 2 µm section with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and use it to select and mark regions of interest.
Macro‑dissect the corresponding areas of the unstained 10 µm sections with a sterile scalpel blade and transfer the tissue fragments into the wells.
Alternatively, place whole 10 µm tissue scrolls directly into a well without macro‑dissection.
Use an antistatic gun to remove static charge from the plate before adding tissue to prevent cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Add lysis reaction mix
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of lysis mix to each well.

substeps.instruction: 80 µl 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0) to give a final concentration of 0.8 M.
10 µl 10 % (w/v) SDS to give a final concentration of 1 %.
5 µl Proteinase K (20 mg/ml) to give a final concentration of 0.5 mg/ml.
5 µl nuclease‑free H₂O.

steps.title: Incubate for lysis and deparaffinization
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and incubate sequentially.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 1 hour at 56 °C.
Incubate overnight (16–24 hours) at 80 °C.

steps.title: Optional RNA digestion
steps.instruction: If downstream applications require RNA removal, treat with RNase A.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 µl RNase A to each well.
Seal the plate, vortex to mix, and centrifuge briefly to collect liquid at the bottom.
Incubate 2 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Melt paraffin in oven
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, place it in a pre‑heated oven and incubate 15 minutes at 56 °C until paraffin is completely molten and dissolved.

steps.title: Column‑based DNA purification
steps.instruction: Purify DNA using a 96‑well DNeasy column plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 mixture of Buffer AL and absolute ethanol (400 µl per well plus 10 % extra, i.e., ~440 µl).
Add 400 µl of the pre‑mixed Buffer AL/ethanol to each well.
Transfer 600 µl of the sample (including Buffer AL/ethanol) onto the DNeasy column plate.
Centrifuge 15 minutes at ≥6,000 g; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µl Buffer AW1; centrifuge 5 minutes at ≥6,000 g; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µl Buffer AW2; centrifuge 15 minutes at ≥6,000 g; discard flow‑through.
Centrifuge the plate 2 minutes at full speed to dry the silica matrix.
Place the column plate on a new collection plate and add 60 µl Buffer AE.
Centrifuge 4 minutes at ≥6,000 g to elute DNA.
Note: If the centrifuge cannot reach 6,000 g, DNA has been successfully isolated at speeds as low as 3,000 g.

steps.title: Bead‑based DNA purification
steps.instruction: Purify DNA using Ampure XP SPRI beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 80 µl Ampure XP SPRI beads to each well (0.8× bead‑to‑sample ratio).
Seal the plate, vortex to mix, and centrifuge 30 seconds at 3,000 g to collect liquid at the bottom.
Place the plate on a magnetic stand and allow beads to pellet on the well walls.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 200 µl 70 % ethanol, wait 30 seconds, then remove ethanol.
Repeat the 70 % ethanol wash once more (total two washes).
Air‑dry the beads for 10 minutes or until completely dry at room temperature.
Add 60 µl nuclease‑free H₂O, resuspend beads by pipetting, and remove the plate from the magnet.
Incubate 10 minutes at room temperature to elute DNA.
Return the plate to the magnet, pellet beads, and transfer the supernatant containing DNA to a fresh DNA lo‑bind plate.
